sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.
Finite-sample differentially private confidence intervals are constructed for the mean of a normal population, with expected-size lower bounds.
Nonparametric frequentist differentially private confidence intervals are constructed for a population median under simple random sampling.

A differentially private heterogeneous-effect meta-learner and privacy-composition analysis are provided, without a finite-sample uniformly honest pointwise H\"older CATE interval or expected-length phase.

Pointwise nonparametric-regression rates are studied under heterogeneous distributed privacy, whose one-server specialization supplies a central-private pointwise-regression comparison, but not for this causal single-curator interval problem.

body.tldr: The raw private higher-order estimator retains its uniform finite-sample remainder bound because clipping occurs only after estimation.  Clipping the released center to \([-1,1]\) cannot increase its error from the bounded causal CATE and makes the reported higher-order set a nonempty random interval on every transcript.  On the uniform-design attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), this interval achieves \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), while the fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval proved on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) remains valid after restriction.  A public selector gives the attainable upper \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\); the uniform-design witness from the ordinary lower bound belongs to the attainable class and gives the stated two-sided nonsharp bracket.  On the unchanged full class, only the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower and \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper are certified, and the sharp private frontier remains the sole open statement.

project_justification.gap: The accepted companion bank entry for central-DP Hölder CATE already proves the corresponding full-class point-risk ordinary lower bound, direct local-polynomial upper bound, and ordinary two-point barrier.  What remained was a finite-sample honest-confidence-interval and mean-length theory, including simultaneous control of higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation, privacy noise, and transcript-wise validity of the reported random interval.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on the uniform-design KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference.  The full-class point-risk endpoints from the accepted companion result serve as supporting inheritance; the present niche is their coverage-facing lift together with a fully private higher-order attainable construction.
project_justification.fill: The paper privatizes every pilot and localized linear and quadratic moment in the attainable higher-order learner, proves a raw-estimator remainder bound for every finite basis rank \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\), with no upper cap relative to effective sample size, using the Gine--Latala--Zinn canonical U-statistic inequality and de la Pena--Montgomery-Smith undecoupling, and clips the released center so the reported interval is nonempty on every transcript.  This gives uniform finite-sample coverage and phase-sensitive mean length at most \(C(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A public deterministic selector chooses between that interval and the restricted direct-regression interval without privacy composition.  The ordinary full-class lower and direct-regression upper exponents are inherited support from the accepted companion point-risk analysis and are lifted here to an honest mean-length bracket; they are not marketed as new endpoints.  The higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), whose nuisance-adaptive and private-Gram confidence frontier remains open.

body.related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983) supplies the consistency-and-ignorability identification framework used to interpret the target as a causal CATE, while Dwork and Roth (2014) supplies the Gaussian-mechanism calibration used in the explicit replacement-DP accountant.  The accepted companion bank entry for central-DP H\"older CATE already establishes the corresponding full-class point-risk ordinary lower and direct local-polynomial upper rates and the ordinary causal two-point barrier; the present paper treats those full-class exponents as supporting inheritance, not as new endpoints.  Karwa and Vadhan (2018) give finite-sample DP confidence intervals for a normal-population mean, and Drechsler, Globus-Harris, McMillan, Sarathy, and Smith (2022) give nonparametric frequentist DP intervals for a population median.  Those established finite-sample CI results do not address a pointwise causal contrast, Hölder smoothing bias, or private nuisance and localized quadratic-moment releases.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) provide a black-box nonparametric private-resampling conversion with asymptotic validity under its assumptions, rather than the finite-sample honest CATE guarantee proved here.  The distinct contribution here is a finite-sample honest-interval and mean-length lift, a fully private higher-order construction on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), a remainder bound for every finite rank \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\) without an upper cap relative to effective sample size, a clipped release that is nonempty on every transcript, and a public selector between two attainable upper constructions.  Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) derive the privacy-free pointwise CATE benchmark and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture; Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective; and Armstrong and Kolesar (2020) motivate fixed-length intervals with explicit worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) study nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands for a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Gine, Latala, and Zinn (2000), Corollary 3.4, together with de la Pena and Montgomery-Smith (1995), Theorem 1, provides the canonical U-statistic moment and undecoupling substrate for the concentration proof.  Schroder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning, and Schroder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Niu et al. (2022) supplies a private heterogeneous-effect meta-learner and composition analysis, while Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024) provide a pointwise nonparametric-regression privacy benchmark in a heterogeneous distributed experiment; neither supplies this single-curator, finite-sample, uniformly honest pointwise CATE interval, its attainable-class selector, or its bracket.  The exact nuisance-adaptive and private-Gram frontier on the unchanged full class remains open.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\) of the clipped quadratic-moment release and is proved only as an attainable-submodel upper cost.  Center clipping is downstream and does not reduce this sensitivity or alter the raw-estimator remainder.  The separate full-class direct-regression release has sensitivity \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\) but incurs armwise bias \(O(h^\beta)\), so it does not determine whether the smoother \(\gamma\)-contrast, the nuisance interaction \(q\), or a stabilized private Gram controls the sharp frontier.  The invalid paired-microcell transport step is not revived.
body.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit clipped-center higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), including the unchanged raw-estimator remainder, nonemptiness on every transcript, and validity for every finite basis rank \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\), with no upper cap relative to effective sample size, together with achieved length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\).  The independent privacy and concentration results remain valid for every finite \(k\ge1\).  The attainable-class nonsharp minimax bracket takes the better of the higher-order interval and the restricted direct-regression interval; its lower witness has uniform design and satisfies every attainable assumption.  The attainable higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  On the full class, the ordinary lower and fixed-dimensional direct-regression upper give \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\) under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\).  Whether either bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains unresolved.  After the present re-certification, \(\mathrm{oeq{:}sharp\text{-}full\text{-}class\text{-}length\text{-}frontier}\) is the only open statement.
